name: type into a real terminal and read its output back
about: krd is a terminal application, so the most valuable second desktop on the VM is a real terminal: a place where a keycode matters, where typing is the only way in, and where the answer is text. This types a command with a unique marker, asserts the marker is in the window's value (a tree dump elides long values, so this searches server-side), then clears the line again. It deliberately does not open a window: a scenario should leave the desktop as it found it, and a cascade of new windows is how a later run ends up typing into the wrong one.

steps.note: keystrokes follow the frontmost app, not the app whose tree you read -- one call buys a whole class of silent failure
start from an empty prompt, so the marker can only come from this run
the marker the shell echoed back is in the window value; `element:` cannot see it because a dump elides values
leave the prompt as it was found
